open_points.subject: EXECUTION_STATUS_CONCLUSIONS for outcome_unknown
open_points.text: “the conclusion each NodeExecution status gives (A13 rules 5 and 7) … a table here keyed by the enumeration, total over its members” contradicts A13 rule 7 and A11 rule 3, where an `outcome_unknown` NodeExecution may wait, succeed, or fail according to its EffectAttempt and resolution.
open_points.question: What value does EXECUTION_STATUS_CONCLUSIONS contain for `outcome_unknown`, and how does run_graph combine that value with effects.operation_element_conclusion after resolution?
options: Use a contextual/sentinel conclusion that requires consulting effects
Map it to waiting while unresolved and explicitly override it after resolution
Exclude operation conclusions from this table, despite the stated totality
open_points.default_guess: Map `outcome_unknown` to a contextual conclusion and let effects.operation_element_conclusion supply waiting, succeeded, or failed.

open_points.subject: NODE_CONCLUSION_EFFECTS taxonomy
open_points.text: “what each node conclusion means for the run and for its dependants … is a correspondence over that taxonomy … a table here keyed by the enumeration, total over its members, whose cells name members” names neither a model enumeration for node conclusions nor enumerations for the run/dependant effects.
open_points.question: What are the exact key and cell types and members of NODE_CONCLUSION_EFFECTS?
options: Add explicit NodeConclusion and dependent/run-effect enumerations to models
Key it by NodeExecution status and use structured cells naming existing RunStatus and NodeExecutionStatus members
Keep these meanings as run_graph logic and remove NODE_CONCLUSION_EFFECTS
open_points.default_guess: Define an explicit NodeConclusion enumeration and a structured effect value covering dependant treatment and run treatment.

open_points.subject: HTTP_METHOD_BODIES cell values
open_points.text: “whether an HTTP method carries a body … is a correspondence … whose cells name members” and “`models`: the row models of its tables and the enumerations their cells name” do not identify any enumeration whose members mean body or no body.
open_points.question: What exact values does HTTP_METHOD_BODIES contain for GET, DELETE, POST, PUT and PATCH?
options: Boolean values, with GET and DELETE false and POST, PUT and PATCH true
A new body-presence enumeration in models
Existing request-body-kind members that also distinguish JSON and multipart
open_points.default_guess: Use booleans: GET and DELETE do not carry a body; POST, PUT and PATCH do.
